drivingQuestion: When may a whole city be included in an eiruv, and does a ladder count as an entrance or a partition?
outcomeNote: Rav Naḥman's reading of Rav is defended via oqimta; Abaye's final position is that the remnant need not be able to join the eiruv

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, סָבֵי דִּידַהּ אָמְרִי לִי: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי מְעָרֵב כּוּלַּהּ. וְאָמֵינָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים הִיא.
segments.en: Rabbi Zeira «said to» Abaye: «The» city «Elders told me» that «Rav Ḥiyya bar Asi» used to «establish an eiruv» for the «entire» city without excluding any section of it, «and I said» to myself: If he would establish an eiruv for the whole city, I can «learn from this» that it was originally «a private city and» later «becomes a public one.» Therefore, it is permitted to establish an eiruv for the entire city.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, לְדִידִי אֲמַרוּ לִי הָנְהוּ סָבֵי: הַהִיא אַשְׁפָּה הֲוָה לַהּ מֵחַד גִּיסָא. וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאִיפַּנְיָא לַהּ אַשְׁפָּה, הָוֵה לַהּ כִּשְׁנֵי פְּתָחִים וַאֲסִיר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו אַדַּעְתַּאי.
segments.en: Abaye «said to him: Those» same «Elders told me» that the reason was different: «There was a particular garbage» dump «on one side» of the public domain, which blocked one of the entrances, leaving only one entrance to the public domain. However, «now that the garbage» dump «has been cleared away, it has two entrances, and» it «is» therefore «prohibited» to establish an eiruv for the whole city without excluding a section from the eiruv. Rabbi Zeira «said to him: It was not on my mind,» i.e., I was unaware that this was the situation.

segments.he: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַמֵּי בַּר אַדָּא הַרְפַּנָּאָה מֵרַבָּה: סוּלָּם מִכָּאן וּפֶתַח מִכָּאן, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב: סוּלָּם תּוֹרַת פֶּתַח עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Rav Ami bar Adda from Harpanya raised a dilemma before Rabba:» If a public domain has «a ladder on one side,» to allow people to scale the wall that blocks it, «and an entrance on the other side, what is» the halakha? Is it considered a public domain that is open on both sides? Rabba «said to him» that «Rav said as follows: A ladder has the status of an entrance,» and therefore the public domain is considered open on both sides.

segments.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב: סוּלָּם תּוֹרַת פֶּתַח עָלָיו, וְתוֹרַת מְחִיצָה עָלָיו. תּוֹרַת מְחִיצָה עָלָיו, כְּדַאֲמַרַן. תּוֹרַת פֶּתַח עָלָיו, בְּסוּלָּם שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת, רָצוּ — אֶחָד מְעָרֵב, רָצוּ — שְׁנַיִם מְעָרְבִין.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman said to them: Do not listen to him. Rav Adda said» that «Rav said as follows: A ladder has the status of an entrance» in certain cases, «and it has the status of a partition» in other cases. «It has the status of a partition» in the case that «we mentioned,» where there is a ladder at the end of a public domain. In this case, the ladder is not considered an entrance and therefore the public domain is considered closed at that end. «It has the status of an entrance in» the case of «a ladder between two courtyards.» If the residents of the courtyards «wish,» they may join the two courtyards by means of the ladder and «establish one eiruv;» if «they wish,» the «two» courtyards may each «establish» a separate «eiruv.»

segments.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר וְאַנְשֵׁי מִרְפֶּסֶת שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Did Rav Naḥman» actually «say this? Didn’t Rav Naḥman say» that «Shmuel said:» With regard to «residents of» the ground floor of «a courtyard and residents of a balcony,» i.e., the floor above the ground floor, «who forgot»

segments.he: וְלֹא עֵירְבוּ, אִם יֵשׁ לִפְנֵיהֶם דַּקָּה אַרְבָּעָה — אֵינָהּ אוֹסֶרֶת, וְאִם לָאו — אוֹסֶרֶת.
segments.en: «and did not establish» a joint «eiruv, if there is a partition four» handbreadths wide «in front of» the entrance to the balcony, the balcony «does not prohibit» the residents of the courtyard from carrying, as each area is considered to be independent. «And if not,» the balcony «prohibits» the residents of the courtyard from carrying in the courtyard. This indicates that a ladder between two courtyards is always considered an entrance, even when that policy leads to a stringent ruling, unless the two areas are separated by a partition.

segments.he: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, בִּדְלֹא גְּבוֹהָ מִרְפֶּסֶת עֲשָׂרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «With what are we dealing here? With» a case where «the balcony is not ten» handbreadths «high» from the ground. Consequently, it does not constitute a domain in its own right, and it is part of the courtyard.

segments.he: וְאִי לֹא גְּבוֹהָ מִרְפֶּסֶת עֲשָׂרָה, כִּי קָא עָבֵיד דַּקָּה, מַאי הָוֵי? בִּמְגוּפֶּפֶת עַד עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, דְּכֵיוָן דְּעָבֵיד דַּקָּה — אִיסְתַּלּוֹקֵי אִיסְתַּלּוּק לֵיהּ מֵהָכָא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If the balcony is not ten» handbreadths «high» and is therefore part of the courtyard, «when one places a partition, what of it?» The balcony should nevertheless be considered part of the courtyard. The Gemara answers: We are dealing here «with» a balcony that is entirely «fenced off» except for a section «up to ten cubits» wide, which serves as an entrance. In that case, «since» the residents of the balcony «place a partition» at this entrance, «they» thereby «remove themselves» entirely «from» the courtyard.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כּוֹתֶל שֶׁרְצָפָהּ בְּסוּלָּמוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ בְּיָתֵר מֵעֶשֶׂר — תּוֹרַת מְחִיצָה עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said:» With regard to «a wall that one lined with ladders, even» along a length of «more than ten» cubits, «it» still retains «the status of a partition.» The ladders do not constitute an opening that is more than ten cubits wide, which would cause the wall to be regarded as breached and would invalidate the wall as a partition.

segments.he: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב בְּרוֹנָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה בְּמַעְצַרְתָּא דְּבֵי רַב חֲנִינָא: מִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל תּוֹרַת מְחִיצָה עָלָיו? וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אַנְשֵׁי מִרְפֶּסֶת וְאַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ וְלֹא עֵירְבוּ, אִם יֵשׁ לְפָנֶיהָ דַּקָּה אַרְבָּעָה אֵינָהּ אוֹסֶרֶת, וְאִם לָאו — אוֹסֶרֶת.
segments.en: «Rav Beruna raised a contradiction to Rav Yehuda in the winepress at Rav Ḥanina’s house: Did Shmuel» actually «say» that such a wall «has the status of a partition? Didn’t Rav Naḥman say» that «Shmuel said:» With regard to «the residents of a balcony and the residents of a courtyard who forgot and did not establish» a joint «eiruv, if there is a partition» four handbreadths wide «in front» of the entrance to the balcony, the balcony «does not prohibit» the residents of the courtyard to carry; «and if not, it prohibits» the residents of the courtyard from carrying? This indicates that a ladder is considered an entrance, as the courtyard and the balcony are considered connected.

segments.he: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, דְּלֹא גְּבוֹהָ מִרְפֶּסֶת עֲשָׂרָה. וְאִי לֹא גְּבוֹהָ מִרְפֶּסֶת עֲשָׂרָה, כִּי עָבֵיד דַּקָּה מַאי הָוֵי? בִּמְגוּפֶּפֶת עַד עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, דְּכֵיוָן דְּעָבֵיד דַּקָּה — אִיסְתַּלּוֹקֵי אִיסְתַּלַּק מֵהָכָא.
segments.en: Rav Yehuda replied in the same manner as above: «With what are we dealing here?» We are dealing «with» a case where «the balcony is not ten» handbreadths «high,» and that is why it is regarded as connected to the courtyard. The Gemara asks: «If the balcony is not ten» handbreadths «high, when he places a partition, what of it?» The balcony should nevertheless be considered part of the courtyard. The Gemara answers: We are dealing here «with» a balcony that is entirely «fenced off» except for a section «up to ten cubits» wide, which serves as an entrance. In that case, «since» the residents of the balcony «place a partition» at this entrance, «they» thereby «remove themselves» entirely «from» the courtyard.

segments.he: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי קָקוּנָאֵי דְּאָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הַב לַן גַּבְרָא דְּלִיעָרֵב לַן מָאתִין. אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְאַבָּיֵי: זִיל עָרֵב לְהוּ, וַחֲזִי דְּלָא מְצַוְוחַתְּ עֲלַהּ בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא. אֲזַל, חֲזָא לְהָנְהוּ בָּתֵּי דִּפְתִיחִי לְנַהֲרָא. אָמַר: הָנֵי לֶהֱוֵי שִׁיּוּר לְמָתָא.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «certain residents of» the city of «Kakunya came before Rav Yosef» and «said to him: Provide us with someone who will establish an eiruv for our city.» The city had originally been a public city and had turned into a private one, requiring that part of the city be excluded from the eiruv. Rav Yosef «said to Abaye: Go, establish an eiruv for them, and see» to it «that there is no outcry against it in the study hall,» i.e., make sure the eiruv is valid beyond any doubt. «He went» and «saw» that «certain houses opened to the river» and not to the city. «He said: Let these» houses serve as «the section excluded» from the eiruv «for the city.»

segments.he: הֲדַר אָמַר: ״אֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶת כּוּלָּהּ״ תְּנַן, [מִכְּלָל] דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְעָירוֹבֵי, מָצֵי מְעָרְבִי. אֶלָּא אֶיעְבֵּיד לְהוּ כַּוֵּוי, דְּאִי בָּעוּ לְעָירוֹבֵי דֶּרֶךְ חַלּוֹנוֹת מָצוּ מְעָרְבִי.
segments.en: Abaye subsequently «retracted» and «said:» This cannot be done, as «we learned» in the mishna: «One may not establish an eiruv for all of it; by inference, if they wanted to establish an eiruv» for the entire city, «they would have been able to establish» such «an eiruv,» if not for the requirement to exclude a section of the city from the eiruv. However, these houses, which do not open to the city, could not have joined in an eiruv with the rest of the city in any case, and therefore they cannot serve as the excluded section. «Rather, I will create windows for them» between the courtyards of their houses and the rest of the city, «so that if they want to establish an eiruv» with the rest of the city «by way of the windows, they can establish» such «an eiruv,» and then these houses will be fit to serve as the excluded section.

segments.he: הֲדַר אָמַר: לָא בָּעֵי, דְּהָא רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ מְעָרֵב לַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ מָחוֹזָא עַרְסְיָיתָא עַרְסְיָיתָא מִשּׁוּם פֵּירָא דְּבֵי תוֹרֵי, דְּכׇל חַד וְחַד הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר לְחַבְרֵיהּ. וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִי בָּעוּ לְעָרוֹבֵי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי, לָא מָצוּ מְעָרְבִי.
segments.en: «He» subsequently «retracted» again and «said:» This «is not necessary, as Rabba bar Avuh established an eiruv for the entire» city of «Meḥoza,» which was a public city that had become a private one, «neighborhood by neighborhood, due to the» fact that the neighborhoods were separated by «ditches» from which «the cattle» would feed. In other words, Rabba bar Avuh established a separate eiruv for each neighborhood without excluding any of them, «as» he maintained that «each one was an excluded section for the other. And although» the neighborhoods «would not have been able to establish an eiruv» together even «if they wanted» to, due to the ditches separating them, the neighborhoods were still able to serve as excluded areas for each other.

segments.he: הֲדַר אָמַר: לָא דָּמֵי. הָתָם, אִי בָּעֵי — לְעָרוֹבֵי דֶּרֶךְ גַּגּוֹת, וְהָנֵי לָא מְעָרְבִי, הִילְכָּךְ נַעְבְּדַן כַּוֵּוי.
segments.en: «He» subsequently «retracted» once again and «said:» The two cases «are not» really «comparable. There,» in Meḥoza, «if they wanted,» they could have «established» a single «eiruv by way of the roofs;» but «these» houses «cannot establish an eiruv» with the other houses of the city, and «therefore we must create windows» for them.

segments.he: הֲדַר אָמַר: כַּוֵּוי נָמֵי לָא בָּעֵי, דְּהָהוּא בֵּי תִיבְנָא דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמָר בַּר פּוֹפִידְתָּא מִפּוּמְבְּדִיתָא, וְשַׁוְּיַהּ שִׁיּוּר לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא.
segments.en: «He» subsequently «retracted» yet again and «said: Windows are also not necessary. As, that storehouse of straw which belonged to Mar bar Pofidata from Pumbedita was designated as the section excluded from» the eiruv arranged for the city of «Pumbedita,» which proves that it is not necessary for the excluded section to be one that could have been included in an eiruv with the rest of the city.

segments.he: אֲמַר, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר לִי מָר: ״חֲזִי דְּלָא מְצַוְוחַתְּ עֲלַהּ בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא״.
segments.en: Abaye «said» to himself: «This is what the Master» meant when he «said to me: See» to it «that there is no outcry against it in the study hall.» Abaye now understood the many factors that had to be considered and how wary one must be of reaching a hasty conclusion.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה, סבי דידה אמרי לי
moves.summary: from Rav Ḥiyya bar Asi's whole-city eiruv he infers the city was private turned public

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה, לדידי אמרו לי הנהו סבי
moves.summary: the elders told him a garbage heap had closed one side; now it is prohibited
moves.about: the whole-city eiruv was due to a garbage heap closing one entrance, not to the city's origin; now it is forbidden

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לאו אדעתאי
moves.summary: he concedes he was unaware of it
moves.about: he was unaware of the garbage heap

moves.cueHe: בעי מיניה רב אמי בר אדא הרפנאה מרבה
moves.summary: ladder on one side, entrance on the other: is it open through?
moves.about: whether a public domain with a ladder at one end and an entrance at the other counts as open through

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה, הכי אמר רב
moves.summary: Rav said a ladder has the status of an entrance
moves.about: the ladder makes it an entrance, so the domain is open through

moves.cueHe: אמר להו רב נחמן: לא תציתו ליה
moves.summary: do not listen to Rabba
moves.about: Rabba's report of Rav that a ladder is always an entrance

moves.cueHe: הכי אמר רב אדא אמר רב
moves.summary: Rav's full tradition: a ladder is a partition at the end of a public domain, an entrance between courtyards
moves.about: a ladder is sometimes an entrance and sometimes a partition

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר רב נחמן הכי? והאמר רב נחמן אמר שמואל
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman's report of Shmuel on balconies implies a ladder is an entrance
moves.about: Rav Naḥman's ladder-as-partition versus his report of Shmuel that a balcony without a partition prohibits the courtyard

moves.cueHe: הכא במאי עסקינן
moves.summary: Shmuel speaks of a balcony under ten handbreadths
moves.about: Shmuel's balcony ruling concerns a balcony less than ten handbreadths high

moves.cueHe: ואי לא גבוה מרפסת עשרה, כי קא עביד דקה, מאי הוי
moves.summary: then what does a partition accomplish?
moves.about: if the balcony is under ten, what does a partition accomplish

moves.cueHe: במגופפת עד עשר אמות
moves.summary: a balcony fenced up to a ten-cubit opening removes itself by the partition
moves.about: a balcony fenced up to a ten-cubit opening, where the partition removes it from the courtyard

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל
moves.summary: a wall lined with ladders remains a partition even beyond ten cubits
moves.about: a wall lined with ladders, even over ten cubits, keeps the status of a partition

moves.cueHe: רמי ליה רב ברונא לרב יהודה
moves.summary: contradicts it with Shmuel's balcony ruling
moves.about: Shmuel's ladder-wall-as-partition versus Shmuel's balcony ruling implying a ladder is an entrance

moves.cueHe: הכא במאי עסקינן
moves.summary: the balcony ruling concerns a balcony under ten

moves.cueHe: ואי לא גבוה מרפסת עשרה, כי עביד דקה מאי הוי
moves.summary: then what does a partition accomplish?
moves.about: if the balcony is under ten, what does a partition accomplish

moves.cueHe: במגופפת עד עשר אמות
moves.summary: a fenced balcony removes itself by the partition
moves.about: a balcony fenced up to a ten-cubit opening

moves.cueHe: הנהו בני קקונאי דאתי לקמיה דרב יוסף
moves.summary: Kakunya's residents ask Rav Yosef for someone to make their eiruv

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה לאביי: זיל ערב להו
moves.summary: sends Abaye, warning him to avoid an outcry in the study hall
moves.about: sends Abaye to make the eiruv, warning against an outcry in the study hall

moves.cueHe: אמר: הני להוי שיור למתא
moves.summary: the river-facing houses will be the remnant

moves.cueHe: הדר אמר: ״אין מערבין את כולה״ תנן
moves.summary: retracts: the remnant must be able to join the eiruv
moves.about: houses that cannot join the eiruv cannot serve as the remnant

moves.cueHe: אלא איעביד להו כווי
moves.summary: he will make windows so the houses could join

moves.cueHe: הדר אמר: לא בעי
